subject: Medford High School Stabbing and Safety Concerns
overview: The School Committee addressed an earlier stabbing at Medford High School, hearing extensive public testimony from students, parents, and community members regarding ongoing safety, bullying, and disciplinary concerns. The Committee voted to convene a special safety meeting before the return to classes in January, while also receiving reports on the newly ratified teachers' contract, elementary reading curriculum, and upcoming state review.

items.title: Consent agenda
items.summary: Approved bills, payrolls, and the regular meeting minutes from December 5, 2022.

items.title: Rules and Policy Subcommittee minutes
items.summary: Tabled the subcommittee minutes to the first meeting in January.

items.title: Superintendent's report and address on high school stabbing
items.summary: Superintendent Edouard-Vincent reported on community holiday drives, recognized fall athletic all-stars, and confirmed that a Medford High School student was hospitalized and stable following a stabbing in a school bathroom earlier that day, with a suspect in police custody.

items.title: School safety discussion, public comment, and special meeting motion
items.summary: Approved a motion to hold an executive session on safety and security protocols followed by a public informational session on student accountability prior to the January return to school. Numerous students, parents, union representatives, and city officials voiced intense frustration over escalating school violence, bathroom safety, communication failures, and disciplinary enforcement.

items.title: Labor relations update
items.summary: Received an update on the newly ratified four-year contract agreement with the Medford Teachers Association, which includes an 11.35 percent budgetary wage impact over four years and prepares for full-day Wednesday schedules starting in the 2023–2024 school year.

items.title: Report on reading instruction curriculum
items.summary: Assistant Superintendent Galusi reviewed elementary literacy instruction, stating that the district does not use three-cueing models and is actively aligning curricula and professional development with the science of reading and enhanced core reading instruction.

items.title: Report on DESE comprehensive district review
items.summary: Assistant Superintendent Cushing outlined the upcoming comprehensive review by the Department of Elementary and Secondary Education and the American Institutes for Research scheduled for December 2023.

items.title: Resolution 2022-54: Support for permanent free school meals
items.summary: Approved a resolution to join the Feed Kids Coalition as a sponsor and urge the Massachusetts Legislature to make universal free school meals permanent.

items.title: Condolences
items.summary: Offered condolences to the families of several community members, district staff relatives, and former educators.
